content:
Ambition is good. But if every achievement immediately becomes a new expectation, when do you actually get to feel proud of yourself?

You finally achieve something you’ve been working towards for months.

For a moment, you feel proud.

And then your mind asks, “What’s next?”

The next exam.
The next internship.
The next milestone.
The next version of yourself you think you need to become.

And just like that, something you once desperately wanted becomes something you’re already expected to have moved past.

Maybe that’s the strange side of ambition.

It keeps us moving forward, but sometimes it moves us so quickly that we forget to look back.

There’s nothing wrong with wanting more. Growth is good. Having bigger goals is good.

But if every achievement becomes the new bare minimum, we can spend years reaching goals without ever feeling like we’ve actually achieved anything.

You can be ambitious and still be proud of where you are.

You can want more without believing that what you have right now isn’t enough.

So maybe, before asking yourself “What’s next?”, ask yourself:

“Have I given myself enough time to appreciate how far I’ve come?” 🤍

Because someday, this version of you might be exactly the version you wished you could become.🌸
